_about: The Story Bible's content, read by src/ui/story-bible.js, src/ui/character-card.js, src/lib/characters.js and src/lib/story.js. Nothing here is stored. `map` says WHICH BLUEPRINT KEYS each card reads and writes (through src/lib/blueprint-store.js — the answer lives in the blueprint blob and nowhere else); `fields` is the wording for each key (taken from steps.feature.json / steps.short.json, minus the A/B/C lettering); `fallback` names feature keys a SHORT project shows after its own. Key strings are a contract with saved work (CLAUDE.md invariant 1): never rename one here.
films_about: A COPY of the four films' identity lines from studies.json (which stays the source: scripts/test-bible.mjs fails if they drift). It exists so the favourite-film picker can draw on Story and Settings without importing the ~100 KB of case studies before first paint (src/ui/fav-film.js).

cards.label: Characters
cards.lead: Who is this about, and who stands in their way? Start with the protagonist and the antagonist; add the rest as they turn up.

cards.label: Conflict
cards.lead: What the story is fought over, and against what. Pick every kind that applies, then say it in one line.

cards.label: Stakes
cards.lead: What is lost if the hero fails: in the world, and inside them.

cards.label: Theme
cards.lead: What the film is about underneath what happens in it.

cards.label: World
cards.lead: Where and when it happens, and the rules of the place.

s3_ext.label: Outer stakes — what happens in the world
s3_ext.placeholder: What does the hero stand to lose in the world?

s3_int.label: Inner stakes — what dies inside the hero
s3_int.placeholder: What part of the hero will die if they fail?

s3_theme.label: Your theme, as a sentence with a verb
s3_theme.placeholder: Your thesis. Something the film is willing to defend.

s3_phil.label: Philosophical stakes — the idea on trial
s3_phil.placeholder: What idea gets disproven if they fail?

s7_rules.label: 3–5 unbreakable rules of your world
s7_rules.placeholder: What is allowed, what is forbidden, what is normal here.

s7_sensory.label: Sensory signature — palette, sound, texture, a recurring object
s7_sensory.placeholder: What does this world look, sound and feel like?

s5_loc.label: Primary location — describe it like a character
s5_loc.placeholder: What does the space look like? What is it for? Who has been in it before? What does it smell like?

s5_time.label: Time of day and weather
s5_time.placeholder: Pick the one that loads the scene with the most meaning. Dawn is not noon; rain is not heat.

s5_anchors.label: Three sensory anchors — sound, texture, recurring object
s5_anchors.placeholder: e.g. SOUND: a ceiling fan one notch slower than it should be. TEXTURE: plastic tablecloth. OBJECT: a glass of water nobody drinks.

s5_rules.label: Rules the world establishes (3–5)
s5_rules.placeholder: What is allowed, what is forbidden, what is normal here. Even a realist short has rules.

conflicts.label: Person vs Person
conflicts.meaning: Someone with their own goal stands in the hero's way.

conflicts.label: Person vs Self
conflicts.meaning: The hero's own fear, flaw or habit is the obstacle.

conflicts.label: Person vs Society
conflicts.meaning: A community, system, law or tradition pushes back.

conflicts.label: Person vs Nature
conflicts.meaning: Weather, wilderness, an animal or a body that will not obey.

conflicts.label: Person vs Fate / the supernatural
conflicts.meaning: Destiny, a curse, a god or a ghost decides what is possible.

conflicts.label: Person vs Technology
conflicts.meaning: A machine, a network or an invention turns on its user.

conflicts.label: Family
conflicts.meaning: Loyalty, duty or blood pulls two ways.

conflicts.label: Time / a deadline
conflicts.meaning: The clock is the opponent: it must be done before it is too late.

conflictLine.label: The central conflict in one line
conflictLine.placeholder: e.g. A cop who cannot forgive himself must stop the one man who knows why.

fields.label: Also written as
fields.placeholder: Other cue names, separated by commas

fields.label: Look
fields.placeholder: What we see first: build, clothes, the thing people notice.

fields.label: Voice notes — how they talk
fields.placeholder: Fast, Chennai college slang, English when he is bluffing

fields.label: Want — what they are after
fields.placeholder: The job, the girl, the respect of his father…

fields.label: Need — what they lack
fields.placeholder: To stop lying to the people who love him

fields.label: Stakes — what they lose if they fail
fields.placeholder: Their home, their name, the one person who believes in them

fields.label: Fear
fields.placeholder: What they would do anything to avoid

fields.label: The lie they believe
fields.placeholder: The false idea they live by

fields.label: Weakness / flaw
fields.placeholder: The habit that keeps getting them hurt

fields.label: Strength / skill
fields.placeholder: What they are genuinely good at

fields.label: Wound — the past event behind it
fields.placeholder: The thing that happened before page one

fields.label: Secret
fields.placeholder: What they hide, and from whom

fields.label: Who they are at the start
Who they are at the end
fields.placeholder: By the final scene, they have become…

fields.label: Arc — how they change
fields.placeholder: From charming liar to a man who owns what he did

slots._about: A character whose role is one of these is the blueprint's own answer for that part: the fields named here are READ AND WRITTEN IN THE BLUEPRINT BLOB, not copied into fms_characters_v1 (no field is stored twice). `fields` is character-field → blueprint key; `short` overrides them for a short-film project, where it names a key. `extras` are further prompts of the same blueprint step, shown on the card and not part of the character record.

short.label: The one obstacle
short.placeholder: Internal (their own flaw, fear, history) or external (someone, something, time). Pick one.

short.label: What we learn about them without dialogue
short.placeholder: Three details an actor and director can show: body language, an object they carry, how they enter a room.

short.label: The turn — the moment that changes everything

feature.label: What they believe
feature.placeholder: Their philosophy, their argument against the hero.

feature.label: Why they are the hero of their own story
feature.placeholder: From where they stand, they are right.

feature.label: The mirror they hold to the protagonist
feature.placeholder: What do they show the hero about themselves?

feature.label: Their one moment of humanity
feature.placeholder: The beat that makes them a person.

feature.label: What they reflect about the hero
The moment they leave, betray or die
What they see that the hero cannot
Their own failure that informs the hero
